'''''Black Box''''' (also known as '''''Black Box: Flight 298''''') is a 2026 American [[Horror film|horror]] [[thriller film]] screenplayed by [[Stephen Susco]] and directed, cinematographed and edited by [[Steven Quale]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Black Box (2026) film |url=https://movieweb.com/tag/movie/black-box-2026/ |website=[[MovieWeb]] |access-date=July 3, 2026}}</ref> It stars [[Tom Brittney]], Holly White, Boadicea Ricketts, Betsy-Blue English, Georgi S. Georgiev, [[Georgina Leonidas]], Vaughn Johseph, [[Weronika Rosati]] and [[Cel Spellman]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Rao |first=Arvind |title=Black Box Trailer Previews Sci-Fi Horror Alien Movie From Final Destination Director |url=https://www.yahoo.com/entertainment/movies/articles/black-box-trailer-previews-sci-160333301.html? |website=[[Yahoo]] |date=June 3, 2026 |access-date=July 3, 2026}}</ref>

== Plot ==
Jeremy Durham is on Vero Airlines Flight 298 from [[Seattle]] to [[New Orleans]], returning with the body of his girlfriend after she died on a hiking trip that they had taken together. Sitting in the back rows of [[economy class]] of the aircraft, Jeremy sees how an elderly, long-bearded man begins coughing nonstop, locking himself in the lavatory. A young girl named Chloe who is on the flight with her mother sits in the opposite row to Jeremy and starts a conversation while waiting to use the bathroom. When the elderly passenger emerges from the stall, he panics, bleeds and dies. Shocked by the sudden death, the two [[flight attendants]] and a female [[air marshal]] try to bring calm after the rest of the passengers begin showing symptoms of illness. 

More than midway into the flight, [[air traffic control]] loses contact with the plane, which is engulfed by a dense cloud filled with [[Extraterrestrial life|aliens]] who attack and possess human bodies. When the creatures attempt to enter the aircraft, a young man who is travelling with two friends takes hold of the exit door and tries to keep it closed. However, one of the aliens gets through the toilet and into the [[First class travel|first-class]] lavatory, attacking and infecting a passenger who subsequently opens the door and gives way to the aliens.  

As the creatures kill most of the passengers, Jeremy, the two flight attendants, the air marshal, a young couple and the girl take refuge in the cargo area. However, an alien uses Chloe's mother's voice to trick her into opening the door, killing her and all but Jeremy and one of the flight attendants. When the crewwoman [[parachutes]] off the plane, she is abducted by the aliens and killed. Meanwhile, Jeremy sees his deceased girlfriend's body, possessed by an alien, talking to him and trying to hug him. Jeremy escapes from the creature and returns to the passengers' area, seeing them all in their seats, staring at him in shock as he is bloodied and with a hammer in his hands. 

The air marshal, presumably infected, tries to stop Jeremy from storming the [[cockpit]]. Aware that these are not humans, Jeremy makes his way through to the cabin and kills the pilots, barricading himself inside and plunging the aircraft nose down with the intent to crash it. As the plane heads down, the [[automatic landing]] system activates, and the aeroplane makes a safe landing. Meanwhile, a [[SWAT]] team storms the aircraft and quickly subdues and arrests Jeremy, who sees the passengers and crew evacuating with serious expressions on their faces. A [[voice-over]] speaking on behalf of the aliens says that they are doing that ([[Aircraft hijacking|hijacking]] planes and taking over human bodies) because they are preparing for a future [[Alien invasion|takeover of Earth]].

==Production==
The film marks director [[Steven Quale]]'s return to the survival horror genre, following his work on ''[[Final Destination 5]]'' and the disaster film ''[[Into the Storm (2014 film)|Into the Storm]]''. The screenplay was penned by [[Stephen Susco]], based on a 2012 short film concept ''The Vessel'' by Clark Baker.<ref>{{cite web|last=Grobar |first=Matt |title=Supernatural Thriller ‘Black Box (Flight 298)’ Adds Eight To Cast |url=https://deadline.com/2024/05/black-box-flight-298-adds-seven-to-cast-1235928713/ |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |date=May 24, 2024 |access-date=July 3, 2026}}</ref><ref name="Lead">{{cite web|last=Bundel |first=Ani |title=Tom Brittney to Lead Supernatural Film 'Black Box (Flight 298)' |url=https://www.tellyvisions.org/tom-brittney-lead-supernatural-film-black-box-flight-298/? |website=Telly Visions |access-date=July 3, 2026}}</ref> Quale took a highly hands-on approach to the production, serving not only as director but also as his own cinematographer and film editor.<ref>{{cite web|last=Hamman |first=Cody |title=Black Box trailer: Final Destination 5 director puts aliens on a plane this July |url=https://www.joblo.com/black-box-trailer/ |website=[[JoBlo.com]] |access-date=July 3, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Cranswick |first=Amie |title=Trailer for horror Black Box teases a flight from hell |url=https://www.flickeringmyth.com/trailer-for-horror-black-box-teases-a-flight-from-hell/ |website=Flickering Myth |date=June 3, 2026 |access-date=July 3, 2026}}</ref>

Principal photography took place primarily on a specialized, enclosed airplane cabin set to maximize the film's claustrophobic atmosphere. The production was handled by Capstone Pictures, Hammerstone Studios, and Inzide Media.<ref>{{cite web|last=Squires |first=John |title=‘Black Box’ from ‘Final Destination 5’ Director and ‘Texas Chainsaw 3D’ Writer Releasing in July [Trailer] |url=https://bloody-disgusting.com/movie/3954332/black-box-from-final-destination-5-director-and-texas-chainsaw-3d-writer-releasing-in-july-trailer/ |website=[[Bloody Disgusting]] |date=June 2, 2026 |access-date=July 3, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Gingold |first=Michael |title=Take a flight of fright with the “BLACK BOX” trailer & poster; release date announced |url=https://rue-morgue.com/take-a-flight-of-fright-with-the-black-box-trailer-release-date-announced/ |website=[[Rue Morgue (magazine)|Rue Morgue]] |date=June 2, 2026 |access-date=July 3, 2026}}</ref>

==Release==
The film had a limited U.S. theatrical release on June 17, 2026, and is scheduled for digital/VOD release on July 7, 2026, by Aura Entertainment.<ref>{{cite web|last=Burnham |first=Christine |title=New Trailer Released For Sci-Fi Thriller ‘BLACK BOX’ |url=https://pophorror.com/new-trailer-released-for-sci-fi-thriller-black-box/ |website=PopHorror |date=June 2, 2026 |access-date=July 3, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Black Box (2026) |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/entertainment/english/movie-details/black-box/movieshow/132114088.cms |website=[[The Times of India]] |access-date=July 3, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Billington |first=Alex |title=Frightening Trailer for 'Black Box' - Extraterrestrials on a Plane Thriller |url=https://www.firstshowing.net/2026/trailer-for-black-box-extraterrestrials-on-plane-thriller/ |website=FIRSTSHOWING.NET |date=June 2, 2026 |access-date=July 3, 2026}}</ref>

==Reception==
Leslie Felperin of ''[[The Guardian]]'' gave the film a rating of 2 out of 5 stars and wrote: "Low-budget chiller leans heavily on tinfoil-hat paranoia to build its reasonably effective suspense."<ref>{{cite web|last=Felperin |first=Leslie |title=Black Box: Flight 298 review – there’s a beastie in the hold in airborne conspiracy horror |url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026/jun/29/black-box-flight-298-review-theres-a-beastie-in-the-hold-in-airborne-conspiracy-horror |website=[[The Guardian]] |date=June 29, 2026 |access-date=July 3, 2026}}</ref>
